text.p: Hungarian home improvement product maker Graboplast will pay a 7.5 percent dividend on its 1996 earnings, as against 6.5 percent on the 1995 profit, the company said.
The 7.5 percent dividend was approved by the annual meeting of Graboplast shareholders on Friday.

In 1996 Graboplast posted a consolidated after-tax profit of 1.397 billion forints on net sales revenues of 15.058 billion forints, up from an after-tax profit of 501.1 million on net sales of 11.591 billion in 1995.
The figures were calculated according to the Hungarian Accounting Standard.

For 1997 the group expects net sales revenues of over 22 billion forints, operating profits of 2.183 billion and pre-tax profit of 2.087 billion, Chairman and CEO Peter Jancso told the shareholders' meeting.
Jancso said the company planned investments worth almost two billion forints.

That amount would be spent on increasing the capacity of Graboplast's textile industry subsidiary Uniontext Kft, the introduction of a new technology at the Grabotext Kft unit, a capital hike at Sotex Rt and infrastructural projects.

The group wishes to continue acquisitions, primarily in the parquetry industry, and Jancso said that a capacity increase in wallpaper production was also necessary as the recently acquired Keszta plant fails to meet expanded demand.
"We work with increased intensity towards acquiring a wallpaper production facility in Eastern Europe," Jancso said.
Graboplast is also considering setting up a joint venture capital company for acquisitions beyond the group's main operating area, he said.
